html.p: Both chart types are ideal for showing performance metrics against defined thresholds or across multiple dimensions simultaneously — common requirements in operational and security dashboards.
A gauge renders a single numeric value as a needle on a dial. The key properties are min, max, and the data array containing a single {value: N, name: 'label'} object.

Use axisLine.lineStyle.color to define threshold-coloured arcs. Each entry is [endFraction, 'color'] where the fraction is a proportion of the full arc (0.0 – 1.0). The example below colours the arc green up to 60%, amber to 85%, and red beyond:
Full viz source for the chart above (copy into a <panel> of your own dashboard):

pre.code:
<viz type="visualization_toolbox.hman">
        <search>
          <query>| makeresults</query>
        </search>
        <option name="visualization_toolbox.hman.dataType">Custom</option>
        <option name="visualization_toolbox.hman.option">
option = {
  title: {
    text: 'CPU Utilisation',
    left: 'center'
  },
  tooltip: {
    formatter: '{a}: {c}%'
  },
  series: [
    {
      name: 'CPU',
      type: 'gauge',
      min: 0,
      max: 100,
      splitNumber: 10,
      axisLine: {
        lineStyle: {
          width: 20,
          color: [
            [0.6,  '#5cb85c'],
            [0.85, '#f0ad4e'],
            [1,    '#d9534f']
          ]
        }
      },
      pointer: {
        itemStyle: {
          color: 'auto'
        }
      },
      axisTick: {
        distance: -25,
        length: 8,
        lineStyle: { color: '#fff', width: 2 }
      },
      splitLine: {
        distance: -30,
        length: 20,
        lineStyle: { color: '#fff', width: 4 }
      },
      axisLabel: {
        color: 'inherit',
        distance: 35,
        fontSize: 12
      },
      detail: {
        valueAnimation: true,
        formatter: '{value}%',
        color: 'inherit',
        fontSize: 22
      },
      data: [
        { value: 73.4, name: 'CPU %' }
      ]
    }
  ]
};
        </option>
        <option name="height">380</option>
        <option name="refresh.display">progressbar</option>
      </viz>

html.p: Add more entries to the data array to render multiple needles on the same dial. This is useful for comparing related metrics side by side — for example, showing CPU, memory, and disk utilisation on one gauge:
Full viz source for the chart above (copy into a <panel> of your own dashboard):

pre.code:
<viz type="visualization_toolbox.hman">
        <search>
          <query>| makeresults</query>
        </search>
        <option name="visualization_toolbox.hman.dataType">Custom</option>
        <option name="visualization_toolbox.hman.option">
option = {
  title: {
    text: 'System Resources',
    left: 'center'
  },
  tooltip: {
    formatter: '{b}: {c}%'
  },
  series: [
    {
      type: 'gauge',
      min: 0,
      max: 100,
      splitNumber: 5,
      radius: '80%',
      axisLine: {
        lineStyle: {
          width: 15,
          color: [
            [0.6,  '#5cb85c'],
            [0.85, '#f0ad4e'],
            [1,    '#d9534f']
          ]
        }
      },
      splitLine: {
        distance: -18,
        length: 15,
        lineStyle: { color: '#fff', width: 3 }
      },
      axisTick: {
        distance: -12,
        length: 8,
        lineStyle: { color: '#fff', width: 2 }
      },
      axisLabel: {
        distance: 20,
        fontSize: 11,
        color: '#555'
      },
      anchor: {
        show: true,
        showAbove: true,
        size: 18,
        itemStyle: { borderWidth: 8 }
      },
      detail: {
        valueAnimation: true,
        formatter: '{value}%',
        fontSize: 14,
        offsetCenter: [0, '70%']
      },
      data: [
        { value: 73, name: 'CPU' },
        { value: 58, name: 'Memory' },
        { value: 41, name: 'Disk' }
      ]
    }
  ]
};
        </option>
        <option name="height">380</option>
        <option name="refresh.display">progressbar</option>
      </viz>

html.p: A radar chart shows values across multiple named axes radiating from a centre point. Define the axes in the radar.indicator array, each with a name and a max. Each series entry holds an array of values in the same order as the indicators.
Multiple data entries are rendered as overlapping polygons, making it easy to compare profiles — for example, two environments or two time periods:
Full viz source for the chart above (copy into a <panel> of your own dashboard):

pre.code:
<viz type="visualization_toolbox.hman">
        <search>
          <query>| makeresults</query>
        </search>
        <option name="visualization_toolbox.hman.dataType">Custom</option>
        <option name="visualization_toolbox.hman.option">
option = {
  title: {
    text: 'Environment Performance Profile',
    left: 'center'
  },
  tooltip: {},
  legend: {
    data: ['Production', 'Staging'],
    bottom: '2%'
  },
  radar: {
    indicator: [
      { name: 'CPU',        max: 100 },
      { name: 'Memory',     max: 100 },
      { name: 'Disk I/O',   max: 100 },
      { name: 'Network',    max: 100 },
      { name: 'Latency',    max: 100 },
      { name: 'Error Rate', max: 100 }
    ],
    radius: '65%'
  },
  series: [
    {
      name: 'Performance',
      type: 'radar',
      data: [
        {
          value: [80, 65, 72, 55, 20, 5],
          name: 'Production',
          areaStyle: { opacity: 0.2 }
        },
        {
          value: [60, 45, 50, 40, 35, 15],
          name: 'Staging',
          areaStyle: { opacity: 0.2 }
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
};
        </option>
        <option name="height">420</option>
        <option name="refresh.display">progressbar</option>
      </viz>
